title: Should I also launch this as an Android and iOS game?
author: sarangbhirad

comments.author: sarangbhirad
comments.body:
Hi readers! 

So I built this game using Claude Code web application. You can also use the desktop app. Works equally well.

I had the idea for this game in my mind for a long time, but since I cannot code, I could never bring it to life.

Until Claude Fable 5.2 launched and people were finally building crazy stuff in single prompt.

So that's when I began.

Here's how it went:

- Opened Claude chat. (Not code yet.)

- Used WhisperFlow to speak out my entire game idea in mind and what all I wanted (different worlds, chasing rocket with shooting power, obstacles you can dodge and obstacles you must shoot, keeping the score, animated graphics, taking design inspiration from games like Angry Birds and Subway Surfers, etc.

- Then I asked Claude to build a detailed PRD (Product Requirement Document) using this information that I can feed as a prompt to Claude code.

- Claude gave me a markdown file (.md), which I downloaded and then pasted into Claude code window and asked to build this web app.

- That's it. Claude took 28 minutes to build the first version of the app which I could play inside a Claude artifact itself. Later I published it to a free domain on vercel, and yesterday I finally purchased the domain and connected it. Now the game is live at riftrungame.com

Hope this workflow helps anyone looking to build a web game using AI and Claude Code.

comments.author: Pik-cher
comments.body: Since it already works in mobile browsers, I'd first check whether phone players actually stick around before taking on native builds. Test touch controls, a few aspect ratios, and pause/resume on real devices; if those feel solid and you see repeat play, then packaging for the stores is a much better bet.
